headline: 5,418 passengers stranded as 51 flights from Dhaka grounded due to Saudi restrictions
summary: Flight disruptions at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport caused by restrictions at Saudi airports, affecting thousands of passengers bound for Riyadh and other destinations.
details: Restrictions at Saudi Arabian airports have led to the disruption of 51 flights from Dhaka, leaving 5,418 passengers stranded.
According to a press release from the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB), the disruptions occurred between Saturday night and Monday afternoon.
Of the total 51 flights, 12 were direct flights to Saudi Arabia, including those operated by Biman Bangladesh Airlines, US-Bangla Airlines, Saudi Arabian Airlines, and Riyadh Air.
The remaining 39 flights were transit flights operated by carriers such as IndiGo, SalamAir, Oman Air, EgyptAir, Emirates, Qatar Airways, and flydubai.
Passengers bound for Riyadh are being redirected via Dammam and Medina to reach their destination.
The disruption has caused significant hardship for migrant workers and travelers, with some reporting being stranded at the airport for hours.
caption:
Over 5,000 passengers are stranded as 51 flights from Dhaka to Saudi Arabia are grounded.

Restrictions at Saudi Arabian airports have led to the disruption of 51 flights from Dhaka, leaving 5,418 passengers stranded.

According to a press release from the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB), the disruptions occurred between Saturday night and Monday afternoon.

Of the total 51 flights, 12 were direct flights to Saudi Arabia, including those operated by Biman Bangladesh Airlines, US-Bangla Airlines, Saudi Arabian Airlines, and Riyadh Air.

The remaining 39 flights were transit flights operated by carriers such as IndiGo, SalamAir, Oman Air, EgyptAir, Emirates, Qatar Airways, and flydubai.

Passengers bound for Riyadh are being redirected via Dammam and Medina to reach their destination.

The disruption has caused significant hardship for migrant workers and travelers, with some reporting being stranded at the airport for hours.

headline_marked: From 4 ducks to a ton: [[Litton Das hits 7th Test century]] in Abu Dhabi
headline: From 4 ducks to a ton: Litton Das hits 7th Test century in Abu Dhabi
summary: After a string of failures, Litton Das delivers a masterclass 102 to steer Bangladesh toward a dominant position against Afghanistan.
details: Litton Das struck his seventh Test hundred on the fourth day of the one-off Test against Afghanistan in Abu Dhabi, marking a significant personal redemption after a difficult phase.
The century came after a personal nightmare where Litton failed to score in all three innings in Australia and registered another duck in the Asian Games T20Is.
In a composed display of class, Litton scored 53 in the first innings and followed it up with a magnificent 102 in the second, hitting 14 boundaries in 117 balls.
He shared a defining 149-run partnership for the seventh wicket with Mehidy Hasan Miraz, further strengthening Bangladesh's lead and putting Afghanistan out of contention.
The innings also saw Litton become the fifth Bangladeshi batter to reach 9,000 runs in international cricket, a landmark achievement in his career.
Despite previous criticism and mounting pressure from media and social media, Litton's performance provided a timely boost to the team's confidence ahead of upcoming challenges.
Litton will now lead Bangladesh in the upcoming tri-nation ODI series featuring Zimbabwe, carrying this regained form into the limited-overs format.
caption:
4 ducks in 5 innings. Then a century. Litton Das just silenced the critics in Abu Dhabi.

Litton Das struck his seventh Test hundred on the fourth day of the one-off Test against Afghanistan in Abu Dhabi, marking a significant personal redemption after a difficult phase.

The century came after a personal nightmare where Litton failed to score in all three innings in Australia and registered another duck in the Asian Games T20Is.

In a composed display of class, Litton scored 53 in the first innings and followed it up with a magnificent 102 in the second, hitting 14 boundaries in 117 balls.

He shared a defining 149-run partnership for the seventh wicket with Mehidy Hasan Miraz, further strengthening Bangladesh's lead and putting Afghanistan out of contention.

The innings also saw Litton become the fifth Bangladeshi batter to reach 9,000 runs in international cricket, a landmark achievement in his career.

Despite previous criticism and mounting pressure from media and social media, Litton's performance provided a timely boost to the team's confidence ahead of upcoming challenges.

Litton will now lead Bangladesh in the upcoming tri-nation ODI series featuring Zimbabwe, carrying this regained form into the limited-overs format.
